runs.text: This is a perfect democracy. Israel is here. Seventy-eight out of a hundred, on the Economist's Democracy Index. What's in the gap? Civil liberties: fifty-six. Political culture: sixty-nine. How the government works: seventy-five. Now zoom out. Critics say Israel is no democracy at all. No democracy looks like this: below forty, where the Economist puts authoritarian regimes. Turkey, forty-three. Lebanon, thirty-six. Jordan, thirty-three. The Emirates, thirty-one. Egypt, twenty-eight. Saudi Arabia, twenty-one. Iran, twenty. Israel is the only democracy on this chart. One honest catch: even Israel is only a flawed democracy, thirty-first in the world. We're not perfect. We know it. But no democracy? We're closer to a perfect one than anyone around us.
